Across my observations at UCSB, I noticed that love often appeared in small and ordinary moments rather than dramatic situations. I saw students talking at activity tables, helping each other study math, paying attention during class, and learning together in supportive environments. Although these moments appeared simple, they demonstrated connection, care, patience and trust among the people on campus. A common theme across all the observations was that students helped each other to feel less isolated by talking, working together, and taking part in activities.
This project changed my understanding of love at UCSB. Before doing my field observations, I mostly thought of love as being about close friendships or romantic relationships. But I also learned that love can be shown through everyday actions that help and support others. The readings in Unit 2 taught me that people often build connections and show care through small actions, rather than big, dramatic gestures.
These observations are important for more than just college life because many people experience stress, loneliness, or pressure in their daily lives. The small acts of attention and support I saw at UCSB show how human connection can help people feel more comfortable, included and supported, even during difficult situations.
